figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Mechanistic insights into verticillene and phomactiene formation. a) Computed energetics for the formation of intermediates and terpene
products. Geometry optimizations and single-point energy calculations were carried out at B3LYP/6–311 + g(d,p) level with PCM solvation model
(solvent = chlorobenzene) and GD3 empirical dispersion. (green ball: hydrogen atom, pink ball: carbon atom) b) Proposed rearranged mechanism
for the formation of 1–4. c) Products produced from mutants of terpene synthases. The ORTEP diagram of the crystal structure of compound 5 is
displayed in the ﬁgure at the 50% probability level, with CCDC number 2480219.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Structural models and active sites of SiPS, LxVS, and AxVS. All structures were predicted by AlphaFold2 and visualized using PyMOL with
the docked intermediate C (cyan). a) The overall structure of SiPS (salmon). b) The overall structure of LxVS (green). c) The overall structure of AxVS
(cyan). d) Comparison of the active site architecture and key divergent residues between SiPS (salmon) and LxVS (green). e) Comparison of the
ampliﬁed active site and key diﬀerent residues in the SiPS (salmon) and AxVS (cyan). f) Comparison of the ampliﬁed active site and key diﬀerent
residues in the LxVS (green) and AxVS (cyan).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Product distribution and metabolite proﬁles of SiPS, PhmA, LxVS, AxVS, and their mutants. a) Relative amounts of terpenes 1–4 produced
by the wild-type enzymes and their respective mutants. Error bars represent the standard deviation of three independent replicates (n = 3). b)
Metabolite proﬁles of selected key mutants, analyzed by GC–MS.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. MD simulations of SiPS and its mutants. a) Representative MD snapshots of the wild type SiPS active site with intermediates C, D, E, and F.
b) Mutant V90N with intermediate C, forming 2. c) Mutant S86Q with intermediate C, forming 3. d) Mutant N311S with intermediate F, forming 4.
The corresponding binding free energies (Gbind) of the enzyme-intermediate complexes are calculated using MM/PBSA, and the conformational
analysis was performed using the following geometric constraints: (α-C)H–O distance ≤2.5 Å and α-C–H–O between 160° and 180°.
